name: Isometric projection
summary: A drawing with three axes at equal angles and one scale, with no vanishing point, so that sizes can be measured.
how: Draw the three axes at 120° to each other; on a pixel grid, use a 2:1 slope (26.57°).
Keep one scale on all three axes and draw no vanishing point.

origin.note: William Farish publishes isometrical perspective as a method for engineering drawing.

adoptions.via: Theo van Doesburg and Cornelis van Eesteren show houses in axonometric drawings.
Sega's Zaxxon is the first arcade game in an isometric view.
Ultimate's Knight Lore builds rooms as isometric boxes on home computers.
Monument Valley uses an orthographic isometric view for impossible architecture.
Isometric illustrations show products, data and offices on tech pages.
Icon packs for product pages and dashboards draw small objects on the isometric grid.

sources.title: William Farish, On Isometrical Perspective (Transactions of the Cambridge Philosophical Society, 1822)
